forbidden.name: no-circular
forbidden.comment: No circular dependency — the repo is deliberately flat (legacy-mcp-inject.js/ctxroute-reset.js → lib-pure.js/lock.js, never the reverse).

forbidden.name: lib-pure-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ lib-pure.js must NEVER import fs/path/child_process — that is the whole point of the module (zero I/O, mutable by Stryker without noise). A dependency here would break the decision/I-O isolation documented in lib-pure.js.

forbidden.name: canary-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ canary.js must NEVER import fs/path/child_process. It DECIDES (alive/dead/undecidable), it does not measure: measurement lives in canary-check.js. Mixing the two would make the verdict untestable and the mutant equivalent — and this module is the ONLY witness of the channel's death.

forbidden.name: lock-stays-io-only
forbidden.comment: lock.js is an I/O module (fs.mkdirSync) — it must not depend on any business logic (lib-pure.js), so it stays reusable independently.

forbidden.name: paths-is-the-only-path-source
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ paths.js = SINGLE SOURCE of the config/docs/state paths. It must not depend on any other module of the repo (otherwise a cycle: everyone imports it). Hooks go through it, never through an ad-hoc path.join(__dirname,...) — two copies of one path diverge silently.

forbidden.name: lib-pure-must-not-know-paths
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ lib-pure.js must stay PURE: paths.js reads process.env/path, importing it would break the decision/I-O isolation (and the Stryker mutant would become noisy).

forbidden.name: sources-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ A SOURCE (payload -> which docs?) is a DECISION, never I/O. Same reason as lib-pure: purity is the CONDITION for Stryker to mutate without equivalent mutants. Mixing fs/path here = losing the mutation signal on the match logic of the 532 rules.

forbidden.name: sources-must-not-know-the-harness
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ A source knows NO harness: it answers a question, decides nothing and writes nowhere. Importing a hook (which speaks the Claude Code dialect) would break the Codex port — the gate translates, the core never does.

forbidden.name: frontmatter-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ PURE parser: the caller reads the file, never the parser. Mixing I/O here would prevent property-based testing (fast-check) from covering everything on generated input.

forbidden.name: loader-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ The loader (corpus -> ordered rules) is a pure DECISION: the caller reads the .md files. Mixing fs/path here = losing mutation on the piece that replaces protected-paths.json at the switchover.

forbidden.name: deadline-stays-standalone
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ deadline.js must depend on NOTHING (like stdin-json.js): it is copyable as-is into any hook, of any project. That is what allows immunizing the 7 hooks of ~/.claude/hooks/ without importing this framework there.

forbidden.name: stdin-json-stays-standalone
forbidden.comment: stdin-json.js is a generic I/O utility (stdin reading) — it must depend on NOTHING else in this repo, so it stays reusable as-is elsewhere.

forbidden.name: lint-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ lint.js = PURE CORE of the fleet audit (mutated by Stryker). The caller reads the disk and provides a STATE; this module DECIDES. Mixing fs/path here would produce equivalent mutants on the only gate that detects dead docs.

forbidden.name: lint-must-not-know-the-harness
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ The lint returns FINDINGS: it prints nothing, never exit()s, formats nothing. The gate takes care of that (same rule as sources/*.js) — which is what makes the Codex port trivial and the core testable without spawning. ⚠️ `lint-corpus` is ITS OWN SHELL: importing it would invert the dependency (the core would know the disk through the back door) and would pull fs/os into the mutated module — the equivalent mutants that `lint-must-stay-pure` already forbids directly.

forbidden.name: collisions-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ collisions.js = PURE CORE of the crossing analysis (mutated by Stryker). The check-collisions.js shell reads the corpus; this module SORTS. Same reason as lint.js: fs/path here = equivalent mutants on the only module that ranks the crossings.

forbidden.name: gate-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ gate.js = THE DECISION of the unified gate (mutated by Stryker). The caller (doc-inject.js) reads corpus/config/state; this module DECIDES. Mixing fs/path here = equivalent mutants on the piece that replaces protect-files' injection at the switchover.

forbidden.name: gate-must-not-know-the-io
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ gate.js knows neither the disk nor the harness through the back door: importing paths/lock/corpus/hooks would pull I/O into the mutated module. It imports ONLY lib-pure (pure → pure).

forbidden.name: explain-stays-out-of-the-hot-path
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ explain.js is a DIAGNOSTIC tool (fail-LOUD, read-only, off the critical path). No gate/guard may import it: a hook is spawned on EVERY tool call of EVERY agent, and a screaming tool has no place in a fail-open path. The reverse direction is the rule: explain consumes collect-core, never the other way around.

forbidden.name: collect-core-must-not-know-the-harness
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ collect-core.js = SHARED collection gate↔explain. It knows no dialect: importing a shell (doc-inject/codex-*) would invert the dependency and bring a harness into the common piece — exactly what the multi-harness port forbids.

forbidden.name: leak-pure-must-stay-pure
forbidden.comment: ⚠️ leak-pure.js must NEVER import fs/path/child_process: it DECIDES whether a text contains personal data, it reads NOTHING. The I/O (git ls-files, private list) lives in leak-gate.test.js. A dependency here would make the decision non-mutable and the gate untestable outside the real repository.
